messages.subject: Using Dates for Axes
parts:
Greetings,

I'm a relative new comer to the R and ggplot2 party (Python tends to
be my default language, but I've been envious of the ggplot2 images
I've seen, so I figured it was time to learn it.)

I have a set of data depicting the number of injuries and fatalities
resulting from January tornadoes. I can create a plot that displays
both injuries and fatalities by year, however I'm simply treating the
year as an integer. When I try to create the same plot treating the
year as POSIXct objects the x-axis has no x-ticks. Any help on what
I'm doing wrong and tips for doing things better would be appreciated.

You can find the code here: https://gist.github.com/783238


Patrick
---

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: Using Dates for Axes
parts:
Hi Patrick,

I think the tick mark issue has to do with a misnamed variable or
possibly the POSIX standard. Unless you will later be dealing with
hours/minutes/seconds, just use the date class.

Everyone is a bit different and has their own style they prefer for
"doing things better". One thing that comes to mind is you might want
to consider a y axis transformation or the little years get completely
overpowered. Here's my take.

Cheers,

Josh


##########################

require(ggplot2)

jan <- structure(list(years = 1950:2009, Injuries = structure(c(15,
11, 15, 21, 2, 0, 12, 34, 17, 5, 4, 0, 31, 15, 10, 9, 0, 290,
0, 241, 7, 27, 147, 56, 28, 380, 9, 0, 46, 1, 1, 0, 36, 7, 0,
0, 0, 1, 93, 64, 37, 20, 2, 3, 8, 76, 58, 60, 10, 346, 22, 12,
0, 0, 3, 31, 41, 39, 52, 0), .Dim = 60L), Fatalities = structure(c(1,
0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 13, 0, 3, 0, 0, 1, 1, 10, 0, 0, 7, 0, 32, 0,
1, 5, 1, 2, 12, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 1, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 0, 0,
1, 0, 0, 0, 3, 1, 2, 0, 18, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 4, 1, 2, 7, 0), .Dim = 60L)),
.Names = c("years", "Injuries", "Fatalities"),
row.names = c(NA, -60L), class = "data.frame")

jan$years <- as.Date(paste(jan$years, "-01-15", sep=""))
jan.melt <- melt(jan, measure.vars=c("Injuries", "Fatalities"))
colnames(jan.melt) <- c("Year", "Casualty", "Count")

xlabs <- scale_x_date(name = "Year", major = "5 years", minor = "1 year")
ylabs <- scale_y_continuous(name = "Count", trans = "sqrt")
leg <- opts(title="January Casualties by Year (1950-2009)",
legend.position=c(0.2, 0.8), legend.background=theme_rect("white"))

## Original
## note the binwidth...dates are stored as numbers, as.Date() by days
## POSIX by seconds, I think, so adjust the binwidth accordingly
ggplot(jan.melt, aes(x = Year, fill = Casualty, weight = Count)) +
geom_histogram(binwidth = 365, position = 'dodge') +
xlabs + ylabs + leg

## A bit of an alternative, I'm not in love with the lines but the
## offset bars distract me---injuries & fatalities happen at once
ggplot(jan.melt, aes(x = Year, y = Count, colour = Casualty)) +
geom_line() +
xlabs + ylabs + leg

messages.subject: Re: Using Dates for Axes
parts:
Thanks, Josh!

I now see the error of an alternative I'd tried. I had originally
tried to use as.Date, but left the binwidth as 1. It brought my
computer to a halt and I couldn't figure out why. Then the figure
contained only one very small line. I didn't realize that as.Date was
stored as days, so I was actually crunching through considerably more
than I needed to. What you suggested was perfect. (I was so focused
on the x-axis I hadn't even begun to try and improve the y-axis.
Thanks for the suggestion there, too!)

Patrick
---
